title: Tsuguharu Foujita's birth chart
metaDescription: Tsuguharu Foujita's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 4.8° Sagittarius. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: Four of the ten placements whose signs are settled stand in Sagittarius — the Sun, the Moon, Mercury and Venus. The placements whose signs could change with an unknown hour are not counted. A cluster that size becomes the section the rest of the chart plays around.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: The Sun sits at 4.8° Sagittarius — the first decan, 0°–10°, which the tradition sub-rules by Jupiter. Degrees matter more than the sign label here: two people born a fortnight apart share Sagittarius and share almost nothing else about where the Sun actually stood.

blocks.title: The personal registers
blocks.text: Mercury holds 18.4° Sagittarius, Venus holds 3.3° Sagittarius, Mars holds 8.8° Capricorn — in the old shorthand, a mind that decides at speaking speed; taste that runs toward the vivid and the immediate; drive that grinds rather than flares.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Venus and Pluto hold the closest angle here — an opposition, 0.3° wide. The scheme reads an opposition as an axis to walk, not a fight to win: the chart keeps both ends lit. Behind it, the Sun conjunction Venus at 1.5°, and the Sun opposition Pluto at 1.8° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. Each angle here was measured at every hour of the civil day and held; whatever the missing clock said, this geometry was in it.

blocks.title: The standing structure
blocks.text: The day-stable angles form no closed figure. Nothing funnels; each aspect is its own negotiation, which the tradition reads as a chart of separate treaties rather than one campaign.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: The classical table has three entries for this chart. Mercury in Sagittarius at 18.4° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain; Mars in Capricorn at 8.8° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best; Saturn in Cancer at 22.0° is in detriment. The old table grades terrain, not talent — a placement in fall works uphill, nothing more.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Of the 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day: 4 in fire, 3 in air, 2 in earth, 1 in water by element, 5 mutable, 4 cardinal, 1 fixed by modality. Fire weights a chart toward initiative — starting, asserting, spending energy to find out what happens. Mercury, Saturn, Neptune and Pluto were retrograde — motion that reverses only from this vantage point, and which the old reading treats as delay used for revision.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Sagittarius for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 13.3° between midnight and midnight. Fast enough that its degree is approximate, slow enough that its sign is not in doubt. At the noon reference it stands at 21.2°.
